legend: A frog is initially at position 0%%ZSMJ0%% on the number line. The frog has two positive integers a%%ZSMJ1%% and b%%ZSMJ2%%. From a position k%%ZSMJ3%%, it can either jump to position k+a%%ZSMJ4%% or k−b%%ZSMJ5%%.

Let f(x)%%ZSMJ6%% be the number of distinct integers the frog can reach if it never jumps on an integer outside the interval [0,x]%%ZSMJ7%%. The frog doesn't need to visit all these integers in one trip, that is, an integer is counted if the frog can somehow reach it if it starts from 0%%ZSMJ8%%.
Given an integer m%%ZSMJ9%%, find ∑mi=0f(i)%%ZSMJ10%%. That is, find the sum of all f(i)%%ZSMJ11%% for i%%ZSMJ12%% from 0%%ZSMJ13%% to m%%ZSMJ14%%.
input: The first line contains three integers m,a,b%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤m≤109,1≤a,b≤105%%ZSMJ16%%).
output: Print a single integer, the desired sum.
note: In the first example, we must find f(0)+f(1)+…+f(7)%%ZSMJ17%%. We have f(0)=1,f(1)=1,f(2)=1,f(3)=1,f(4)=1,f(5)=3,f(6)=3,f(7)=8%%ZSMJ18%%. The sum of these values is 19%%ZSMJ19%%.
In the second example, we have f(i)=i+1%%ZSMJ20%%, so we want to find ∑109i=0i+1%%ZSMJ21%%.
In the third example, the frog can't make any jumps in any case.
